idiom_name: class method composed of calls to other methods (this.step() / #step())
implementation_notes: A class method whose body only calls other methods of the same class is the plain JavaScript form; since ES2022 the steps can be true private methods (#reserveStock()) that are not part of the object's public shape and cannot be reached from outside, while older code marks them with an underscore by convention because this lookups are dynamic. Module-scoped functions are the alternative when a step needs no instance state - they are not on the prototype and are shared by every instance.
pitfalls: Methods are looked up on this at call time: extracting one (const run = cart.run; run()) loses the receiver and throws because this is undefined in modules/strict mode.
#private methods are brand-checked: calling a private step on an object that merely mimics the class (a plain object or a Proxy) raises a TypeError.
Arrow-function class fields capture this and are per-instance, so a step written as a field allocates a closure per object instead of being shared on the prototype.
